items.title: Dow & S&P 500 futures reached all-time highs as traders prepared for CPI data.
items.excerpt: Equity Index futures saw a divergence in performance, with the Dow and S P reaching all-time highs while the Nasdaq-100 and Russell lagged. U.S. Treasury yields and the U.S. dollar moved lower, providing fundamental context for the coming week. Looking ahead, market participants are closely monitoring the upcoming U.S. CPI report, where core CPI is expected to rise 0.2% month-over-month. Earnings season continues with 184 major companies slated to report, including Berkshire Hathaway and Cisco. Additionally, the U.S. Treasury plans to auction 125 billion dollars across 3-year, 10-Year, and 30-year maturities, while a slew of global economic data will keep traders focused.

items.title: Euro futures rally to eight-week high on shifting rate outlook.
items.excerpt: Euro futures experienced a notable rally, reaching an eight-week high and pushing toward the strongest close since mid-June. The September contract saw positive momentum, setting up for a second consecutive week of higher prices. Mixed economic data out of Germany provided underlying support, with factory orders rising 3.1% and industrial production increasing for a third consecutive month, despite a narrowing trade surplus. Furthermore, shifting rate differentials continue to favor the euro. While the ECB held its key rate at 2.25% in July following a June hike, markets anticipate potential further tightening. items.title: AI’s next phase: Investing beyond the bottlenecks
items.excerpt: Key points: Cheaper AI strengthens the adoption story. Falling model and inference costs should allow AI to spread across more businesses, employees and everyday applications. That is positive for overall usage, even if it puts pressure on the pricing power of model developers and some hardware suppliers. More intentional AI capex does not mean the end of hardware demand. Hyperscalers will keep spending, but they will increasingly optimise what hardware they buy, where they deploy it and what return it generates. The winners may shift from broad hardware exposure towards specialised bottlenecks and efficient infrastructure. items.title: Canadian Dollar futures rebound as U.S. hiring cools.
items.excerpt: Canadian Dollar futures rotated higher after three consecutive sessions of losses, buoyed by a widening Canadian trade surplus and weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data. Statistics Canada reported the June merchandise trade surplus expanded to 3.86 billion Canadian dollars, driven by a 16.5% surge in metals and mineral exports led by gold. In the U.S., ADP private payrolls grew by just 44,000, while ISM Services employment slipped into contraction territory. The combination of soft U.S. labor data and persistent inflation pressure weighed on the greenback, providing support for the loonie.

items.title: Australian Dollar futures rebound toward multi-month highs.
items.excerpt: Dan Deming discusses the recent price action in Australian Dollar futures, highlighting a swift recovery from recent selling pressure. The currency is demonstrating relative strength compared to other major FX markets, largely driven by stronger-than-expected Australian household data and persistent weakness in the U.S. dollar. Deming notes that the Australian dollar is pushing toward one-and-a-half-month highs, with 0.706 acting as the next critical upside target. A successful breakout above this level could drive prices to their highest point since early June. The broader currency complex remains somewhat mixed, though most majors are leaning higher against the softer greenback.
